summary: Flexible green strap algae attach to illuminated coastal rock. Broad holdfasts resist surge and mucilage delays drying. For generation and play, exposed blades tolerate at most four consecutive standard hours of warm, clear, drying emersion before severe desiccation damage; shelter and retained water can prolong survival. Beds thin to zero where time-integrated daylight no longer supports positive net growth at the sunken cave entrance, a placement boundary rather than a fixed canon depth (F9, F13, F20).

chains.trait: Flow-reconfiguring straps attached by broad holdfasts
links: The tidal shelf provides alternating inundation, while local currents and waves impose variable loads whose speeds are not specified by tidal range.
At comparable projected area, water drag rises approximately with the square of flow speed.
Flexible straps align with flow and reduce projected area instead of resisting it rigidly.
Broad holdfasts distribute attachment forces over stable rock, but either attachment or substrate can still fail.
chains.play: Read local flow direction from moving blades and inspect the bed for marine feeders without treating tidal range as current speed.
chains.weakness: Exceptional surge tears blades or exceeds attachment strength; weathered rock can break beneath an intact holdfast.
observe: Blades flatten and reverse with surge.
Torn ribbons drift away from surviving holdfasts.
Detached holdfasts sometimes retain fragments of broken substrate.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Underwater loading comes from water flow. Shelf tidal range is neither wave height nor a universal current speed. Strict review (2026-11-19): revised: The rewrite removes turbidity as evidence for loading and separates flow reconfiguration and attachment from the independent shelter created by a bed. Residual: F13 supports alternating inundation, and F21 provides rocky coastal settings. The chain correctly derives loading from water velocity rather than atmospheric density or tidal range. Flexible reconfiguration and distributed attachment are coherent mechanisms. Residual weakness: broad holdfasts require adequate adhesion and cohesive substrate; oscillatory surge can produce acceleration and transient loads beyond the approximate steady drag relationship.

analogues.organism: Ulva and flexible bladed marine macroalgae
analogues.mechanism: Flexible thalli reconfigure in moving water, moderating loads while retaining photosynthetic area.

chains.trait: Thin illuminated blades with moisture-retaining mucilage
links: Turbid water restricts useful light to shallow illuminated sites.
Thin blades intercept light near the surface.
Mucilage and overlapping blades slow water loss during ebb.
Continued warm, clear exposure exhausts retained moisture and damages tissue.
chains.play: Gather fresh blades early in ebb; inspect stranded tips before offering them as food.
chains.weakness: The exposed-blade drying limit is four consecutive local hours in warm, clear conditions; burial and permanent darkness also prevent productive growth.
observe: Fresh ribbons cling together in a slippery film.
After prolonged clear exposure, upper tips become dull and brittle.
Attached living blades disappear at the cave's daylight threshold.

plausibility.judge: strict review: sol (codex) + DeepSeek; chair sol
plausibility.summary: Four hours is a fictional gameplay calibration for drying exposure, not an experimentally established tolerance or an unconditional biological timer. Pools, fog and shade alter drying; living beds remain within sufficient daylight. Strict review (2026-11-19): Residual: F20's turbid shallows support a restricted photic habitat, and mucilage plus overlapping blades can delay drying. Residual weakness: underwater visibility below 10 m is not a photosynthetic depth limit, and four hours is a declared gameplay calibration rather than a physiological consequence of F13 or F20. The explicit daylight and retained-water conditions keep the chain defensible.

analogues.organism: Intertidal Ulva and other periodically exposed seaweeds
analogues.mechanism: Water retention and physiological stress resistance permit finite emersion tolerance and contribute to shore zonation.

gameplay.cover: Submerged visual shelter for small aquatic creatures.
gameplay.notes: Zancuda eats blades; sifon, cuarteta and brujula consume associated suspended food or detritus. Dull brown stranded tissue indicates deterioration rather than an intrinsic poison. Waterborne propagules replace pollination. The four-hour gameplay limit means four standard hours of warm, clear, drying exposure; local hours in the unchanged chain use the same standard hour within the 26-hour day. Fog, shade, pools, splash and retained water can prolong survival. Algae do not make incoming tides safe.

relations.note: Feeds on plankton and drifting carcass bits behind fronds.
Sweeps suspended food from sheltered gaps.
Collects detritus and suspension food around holdfasts.
A vertical zonation neighbour: the terrestrial shrub occupies spray-zone ground above the intertidal algae.

generator.trunk: No trunk; flexible stipes attach by holdfasts 5–15 cm across. Height denotes extended thallus length.

leaf.type: Thin strap-like thallus blade; no true leaves

overlay_rules: Overlapping wet blades appear dark green.

placement.slope: Stable illuminated benches, pool sides and shelves on 0–45 degree slopes.
placement.wetness: Treat altitude as a candidate envelope relative to mean sea level, not a bed mask. Dense intertidal beds follow local low- and high-water levels; retain deeper patches only with adequate light and upper patches only in wetted pools or regularly splashed refuges. Exclude sites routinely exceeding four standard hours of warm, clear, drying emersion without retained water.
placement.soil: Stable rock without persistent burial; require time-integrated light sufficient for positive net growth after accounting for depth, turbidity and cave shading.
placement.fog: Slows drying but cannot replace tidal wetting.
placement.density: Dense sheltered photic beds thinning to zero where the light budget no longer supports positive net growth; visible daylight alone is insufficient.

generator.seasonal: Expands in cool favourable periods; storms and prolonged summer emersion reduce exposed beds.
generator.wind_response: Submerged blades follow water flow; exposed ribbons lie against rock and dry faster in wind.
generator.attachment_failure: Detach when local hydrodynamic load exceeds holdfast attachment capacity or substrate fracture capacity; numerical thresholds require calibration rather than inference from holdfast diameter.

journal.en: The sea lays its ribbons down, then lifts them again. Eat while the stones are showing.
journal.es: El mar deja sus cintas y vuelve a levantarlas. Come mientras se vean las piedras.

observe: A green carpet at ebb becomes a waving bed at flood.
Zancuda leaves cropped ends along shallow margins.
Loose fragments can occur beyond the last living attached blades.
secrets: Attached living blades identify the illuminated cave fringe.
Drifting ribbons reveal current direction without predicting the next tidal turn.
